frequency_question: How often does a central bank successfully plan, clear internal governance, prepare banking IT systems, and issue an implementation circular for an extraordinary liquidity management tool within a sub-six-month window?
membership_rule: Includes any formal regulatory announcement and rollout of a targeted, temporary incremental reserve ratio or equivalent non-standard liquidity absorption mandate by the Reserve Bank of India or comparable monetary authorities during surplus liquidity regimes; excludes routine repo/reverse-repo rate adjustments or permanent statutory reserve ratio changes.
provenance_note: claims 150 cases from only 2 named (75.0x); beyond 3.0x the skeleton is not carrying the estimate
coverage_note: 2 named formal iCRR adoptions by RBI in modern history; total relevant major surplus absorption regulatory pivots total 2.
known_gaps: Excludes minor adjustments to standard CRR which do not use the 'incremental' or temporary liquidity-locking nomenclature.
skeleton: RBI monetary policy committee decision cycles per year (6) multiplied by extraordinary liquidity surplus episodes requiring non-standard instruments over a 25-year structural review period (2).
multiplier: 2 historical adoptions of iCRR across multiple liquidity management episodes out of approximately 150 total bi-monthly policy review cycles.
validity_reason: Central banking operational frameworks and statutory powers regarding reserve ratios remain governed by the same legislative acts (RBI Act 1934) through the end of the decade.
